column2: Hi [baseline_arm_1][first_name], it's the MICA Team checking in.
Amazing job staying alcohol-free this week! Your body and mind will thank you for it
Staying alcohol-free this week took effort and intention. Give yourself credit for the choices you made along the way.
Incredible! You made a smart choice this week, and it's a big step toward your goals.
Awesome work! Staying alcohol-free shows your strength and commitment-keep it up!
Well done! Skipping alcohol this week is a great way to prioritize your well-being.
That's fantastic! You're proving to yourself that you can make choices that align with your goals.
Congrats on sticking to your plan this week! Your body and mind will feel the benefits!
You crushed it! Another alcohol-free week is another step toward feeling your best.
Well done on not drinking this week! It's a big accomplishment-celebrate that!
Awesome decision! You're showing how much control and strength you have-keep up the good work!
Fantastic! By choosing not to drink, you're setting yourself up for long-term health and success.
Great job! You made a choice that supports your goals and shows your dedication to change
Nice work this week. You stayed within lower-risk drinking levels, which shows awareness and control over your choices.
You reported drinking this week while staying below higher-risk levels. Think about what helped you keep your drinking where you wanted it.
Staying within your limits is an accomplishment. The choices you made along the way helped make that happen.
It sounds like you found a balance that worked for you this week. Taking time to notice what contributed to that success can help in the future.
Great job staying within lower-risk drinking guidelines. Small decisions can make a big difference over time.
This week shows that drinking and staying within your goals can go together. Reflect on what strategies helped you stay on track.
You remained below higher-risk drinking levels this week. That reflects thoughtful choices and attention to your goals.
Every week that you stay within your limits helps build confidence in your ability to manage your drinking.
You demonstrated control over your alcohol use this week. Give yourself credit for the decisions that supported that outcome.
Staying within lower-risk drinking levels can support better health, sleep, mood, and energy.
You met a goal that many people find challenging—enjoying alcohol while keeping it within boundaries that feel right for you.
Looking ahead, try to continue making choices that fit with your goals around drinking.
This week’s drinking was in the range considered unhealthy. Taking a moment to consider how that fits with your personal goals may be worthwhile.
Drinking above recommended limits can increase the risk of health, relationship, and daily life problems over time. Small changes can make a meaningful difference.
Sometimes drinking patterns move us closer to our goals, and sometimes they move us farther away. This week may be an opportunity to reflect on what matters most to you.
The choices made this week do not define the future. Every week offers a new chance to move toward the life you want.
Drinking above lower-risk levels is common, but it can carry consequences that are easy to overlook in the moment and harder to ignore over time.
Many people find that their drinking does not always align with the goals they have for their health, energy, relationships, or future.
Lasting change often begins with noticing patterns honestly and without judgment. Awareness is an important first step.
Alcohol can offer short-term benefits while also creating costs that may not become apparent until later. Both sides are worth keeping in mind.
Reflecting on how alcohol fits into your priorities can help guide future choices in a direction that feels right for you.
Progress is not measured by perfection. It is measured by paying attention, learning, and continuing to move toward what matters most.
Drinking above lower-risk levels may increase the likelihood of alcohol-related consequences. Recognizing that risk can be an important part of making informed decisions.
Your goals, values, and priorities are uniquely your own. Taking time to consider whether your drinking reflects those priorities can be a powerful exercise.
Great! Thanks for letting us know.
Change often begins with paying attention rather than making a commitment. Taking time to reflect on your drinking can still be valuable.
Not everyone is ready to make a change immediately. Many people spend time weighing what they enjoy about drinking against what concerns them.
Choosing not to set a goal today does not mean you have closed the door on change in the future.
It can be difficult to think about changing a behavior that serves an important role in your life. Taking time to understand that role can be useful.
Many people feel uncertain about making changes to their drinking. Ambivalence is a normal part of the process.
You may not be ready to set a limit right now, but continuing to notice how alcohol affects your health, relationships, and daily life can provide valuable insight.
Change is most likely to last when it comes from your own reasons and priorities rather than pressure from others.
Deciding not to set a goal today is still a decision worth acknowledging. It reflects where you are right now in thinking about your drinking.
Sometimes the most important step is simply becoming more aware of how drinking fits into the life you want for yourself.
Many people find that their motivation for change develops gradually over time rather than all at once.
Whether or not you decide to make changes in the future, paying attention to the connection between your drinking and your personal goals can be informative.
Taking time to consider both the benefits and costs of drinking can help clarify what matters most to you
Great decision! Setting a drinking limit is a powerful way to stay in control. Alternating alcoholic drinks with water can make it easier to stick to your plan and feel better the next day.
Nice work setting a goal. People are often more successful when they decide in advance how many drinks they'll have rather than making decisions in the moment.
You’ve already taken an important step by choosing a limit. Slowing down and taking time between drinks can help your choices stay aligned with your goal.
Excellent choice. Staying in control of your own drink purchases can make it easier to track your drinking and stick with the limit you set.
Way to go! Eating before or while drinking can help reduce the effects of alcohol and make it easier to pace yourself throughout the evening.
Setting a goal shows commitment to yourself. Keeping a simple count of your drinks on your phone can help you stay aware of your progress.
Great plan. A quick check-in with yourself during the evening can help you decide whether your drinking is still matching the goal you set.
Nice work taking this step. Choosing beverages with lower alcohol content can help you enjoy social situations while staying within your limit.
You’ve made a thoughtful decision. Spending time with people who respect your goals can make it easier to follow through on them.
Setting a limit is a sign that you care about your health and well-being. Mixing in non-alcoholic drinks can help you stay on track and stay hydrated.
Great job committing to a goal. Removing easy opportunities to drink more than planned—such as carrying only enough money for your intended drinks—can support your success.
Well done. Deciding ahead of time how you’ll respond if offered another drink can make it easier to stay confident and stick with the choice you already made.
This completes the text messaging intervention part of the MICA study.
